Killing Azure Data Studio in favour of using this extension with vanilla-VS Code was a terrible decision for usability. I understand the other forces that would have led to the decision, but interaction with SQL Servers and SQL programming is fundamentally quite different to other kinds of usage of VS Code. SSMS has gotten markedly better with v21 and especially v22, but I still much prefer the VS Code / electron style interface when I'm doing more SQL code-heavy work over server administration. (Like churning out loads of exploratory ad-hoc analytic SQL queries.)  When I am launching VS Code with a SQL-centric task in mind, I want the UI to be heavily biased towards SQL-centric interpretations of what I'm trying to do. Just like how ADS used to work, and how SSMS does work.  Simple examples: if I've connected to a server in the object explorer, and do Ctrl+N, I want that new tab to immediately pick up my SQL connection and assume I am about to write some SQL. I don't want to have to connect in each tab manually, and to set the language to T-SQL manually. If I've connected to 2+ servers already in the object explorer and do Ctrl+N, I either want a predicable decision about which to connect to automatically, or a focused UX that lets me choose which of the active connections this tab should use - but again, minimal interaction to achieve the result. If there's already a tab in focus that has a SQL connection and using SQL language mode, and I do Ctrl+N from there, the new tab should definitely inherit the settings from the existing tab.   I know there are right-click options from the object explorer but I don't always want to use my mouse, nor should I have to.   This Ctrl+N behaviour isn't the only thing that frustrates me about using VS Code + MSSQL extension, but it's the easiest one to think of. There needs to be a holistic review of the UX specialisations that ADS had, and that SSMS has, and that needs to be implemented thoroughly here too.   Oh and also, it's bl**dy iritating that restarting extensions (which VS Code prompts me to do seemingly every day, a pain point of its own, broader than just this extension) kills all active SQL connections etc. There needs to be some kind of guard against that - an "are you sure" dialog if there's anything active in the MSSSQL extension, or have that extension just not restart this way.
